invariants_checked: no panic or data race under OS-thread contention
every commit advances the root to a complete transaction boundary
the recovered index equals the live index (canonical digest)
reads by inode survive unlink (non-withdrawal, open-handle semantics)
manifestation publication never changes logical read output
root pins are released and pinned roots stay valid
a reader never observes a torn/partial state: every read returns a whole committed version
readers are not blocked by another reader's physical I/O
concurrent reads scale past a single reader (throughput)

model_checking.reason: The real shared state is a std::sync::Mutex<BTreeMap>, a parking_lot::RwLock+Condvar worker pool, and &mut-borrow serialised commits plus real fsync I/O; Loom models only substituted std::sync primitives and pure in-memory state, so modelling it would test a different program. The directive's explicit fallback (stress tests) is used instead.

tests.name: readers_scale_and_are_not_blocked_by_other_readers_io
tests.note: throughput vs 1/2/4/8/16 readers, concurrent immutable read views vs the global core lock; evidence/performance/reader-scaling.json
